author: misilva73
content:
If I recall correctly,  we can get three main things that we currently don't have: 
1. A more realistic environment where we also account for CL processing load
3. Long-living load tests (i.e., we spam the network for many consecutive blocks instead of running a single block at client start)
2. Syncing benchmarks

Am I missing something, <@508125616940515329> ?

author: jochembrouwer
content:
If we compare to benchmarkoor then yes those points listed are correct. The main point is that in benchmarkoor we have a mock-CL and here we have an actual CL. Also note that in benchmarkoor we *re-execute blocks*. On the live network, we also test the block builder (somewhat), which is not part of benchmarkoor. (That is EL-only block *re-execution* what we bench)
On the live network, especially the propagation times are interesting. If we hit a slow block, we can see how this spreads over the network (or not), and if this has any adverse effects.
The interesting part here, which is what we should test, is how the mix of clients performs in the benchmark situations. If 1 client is slow in a particular situation then another client could be fast in this situation. So they balance each other out 🤔 
What I think what we should do is to hook up the benchmark generator on top of this live network. Via that, we can run the benchmarks via the block builder, and now test this over the network.
I'll prep using buildoor for this 👍  

For the syncing benchmarks, this is also a good point, clients can choose to re-execute blocks in Glamsterdam if they have the state for a specific Glamsterdam block, but they can also choose to directly apply the BAL state diff on top of the previous block to land at the correct state. This speeds up the sync time 😄
